chapters.title: Elijah and Ahaziah
chapters.html:
2 Kings 1

Ahaziah Inquires of Baal-zebub

1After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

2Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers, telling them, "Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this injury."

3But the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?

4Now therefore thus says the LORD: You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'" So Elijah went.

5The messengers returned to the king, and he said to them, "Why have you come back?"

6They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you, and say to him, "Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die."'"

7He said to them, "What kind of man was he who came up to meet you and told you these things?"

8They answered him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist." He said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."

Fire from Heaven

9Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. He went up to him, and there he was, sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"

10But Elijah answered the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

11Again the king sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. He answered and said to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: 'Come down quickly!'"

12But Elijah answered them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

13Again the king sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, "Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.

14Fire has come down from heaven and consumed the two former captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your sight."

15Then the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he arose and went down with him to the king,

16and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of His word? — therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'"

17So he died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because he had no son.

18The rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

Notes

  • v2 "Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron" — Ba'al Zevuv, lord of flies, the god of a Philistine city. In the Gospels the Pharisees say Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons (Matthew 12:24).

  • vv2–3 "he sent messengers… the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah… to meet the messengers of the king" — mal'akhim and mal'akh YHWH, the same word for the king's envoys and the LORD's. The king sends his to Ekron; the LORD sends His to stop them.

  • vv3, 6, 16 "Is it because there is no God in Israel" — ha-mibbeli ein Elohim be-Yisra'el, asked three times, each time with the same sentence of death after it.

  • vv4, 6, 16 "You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up" — alita… lo tered: the king has gone up to his bed and will not come down; Elijah on the hill is told to come down (vv9, 11), and goes down only at the LORD's word (v15).

  • v8 "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist" — ish ba'al se'ar, a man of hair. Elijah's garment is his adderet, cloak (1 Kings 19:13, 19), and Zechariah speaks of the prophets' adderet se'ar, hairy cloak (Zechariah 13:4). John the Baptist wore clothing of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist (Matthew 3:4).

  • vv10, 12 "If I am a man of God, let fire come down" — ish and esh, man and fire, near in sound. When a Samaritan village would not receive Jesus, James and John asked, Lord, do you want us to bid fire come down from heaven and consume them? (Luke 9:54).

  • v13 "please let my life… be precious in your sight" — the third captain asks instead of commanding, and lives.

  • v15 "the messenger of the LORD said to Elijah… do not be afraid of him" — the prophet goes to the king who sought him, at the LORD's word.

  • v17 "Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat" — two kings named Jehoram, one in Israel and one in Judah. Later the text puts Jehoram of Israel's accession in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat (3:1); both dates stand in the text. Because he had no son: his brother succeeded him.

chapters.title: Elijah Taken Up
chapters.html:
2 Kings 2

From Gilgal to the Jordan

1And it came to pass, when the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, that Elijah and Elisha were going from Gilgal.

2Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.

3The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from over your head?" He said, "Yes, I know it; keep silent."

4Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

5The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho came near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD will take your master from over your head?" He answered, "Yes, I know it; keep silent."

6Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.

7Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood at a distance facing them, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

8Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water, and the water was divided to one side and to the other, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

The Chariot of Fire

9And it came to pass, when they had crossed, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me."

10He said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me as I am being taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so."

11And it came to pass, as they were still going on and talking, that a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven.

12Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" He saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.

13He took up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

14He took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the water and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he too had struck the water, it was divided to one side and to the other, and Elisha crossed over.

Elisha at Jericho

15When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from a distance, they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

16They said to him, "Your servants have with them fifty strong men. Please let them go and look for your master. It may be that the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and cast him on some mountain or into some valley." He said, "You shall not send them."

17But when they urged him until he was ashamed, he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.

18They came back to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"

19The men of the city said to Elisha, "The situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage."

20He said, "Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.

21Then he went to the spring of water and threw salt in it and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'I have healed this water; from now on neither death nor miscarriage shall come from it.'"

22So the water has been healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.

The Boys of Bethel

23He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up on the way, some small boys came out of the city and mocked him, saying to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"

24He turned around, looked at them and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two she-bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the boys.

25From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

Notes

  • vv2, 4, 6 "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you" — three times Elijah tells Elisha to stay, and three times Elisha swears the same oath. At Bethel and Jericho the sons of the prophets ask him the same question, and he gives the same answer.

  • v3 "the LORD will take your master from over your head" — me-al roshekha, from over your head, from his place above you.

  • vv8, 14 "struck the water… crossed over on dry ground" — ba-charavah, the word of the crossing of the sea, the sons of Israel came into the middle of the sea on dry ground (Exodus 14:22), and of the Jordan under Joshua (Joshua 3:17). Elijah crosses east as Joshua crossed west; Elisha comes back across as Joshua did.

  • v9 "a double portion of your spirit" — pi shenayim, the firstborn's share of an inheritance, a double portion of all that he has (Deuteronomy 21:17). Elisha asks to be Elijah's heir, not to be twice Elijah.

  • v11 "a chariot of fire and horses of fire… Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven" — bi-se'arah, in a storm wind. The text says the chariot came between them; it was the whirlwind that carried Elijah up.

  • v12 "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" — the same cry King Joash will raise at Elisha's deathbed (13:14).

  • vv15–16 "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha… the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up" — Elijah's own spirit, lowercase; ruach YHWH, capital, as fixed. The sons of the prophets feared the Spirit might carry Elijah off, as Obadiah had (1 Kings 18:12).

  • vv19–22 "the land causes miscarriage… neither death nor miscarriage" — meshakkelet, from shakhal, to be bereaved of children. Salt in a new bowl, and the word I have healed.

  • v23 "some small boys… Go up, baldhead!" — ne'arim qetannim; in v24 they are yeladim, children or youths. Go up, aleh, is the verb of Elijah's going up (vv1, 11).

  • v24 "two she-bears… tore forty-two of the boys" — va-tevaqqa'nah, tore open. The text does not say that the boys died.
